title: DHS Mandates Body Cameras on Every ICE Arrest Team After Two Fatal Camerless Shootings
excerpt: Following the fatal ICE shootings in Houston and Maine — both lacking body camera footage — DHS announced that every ICE arrest team must include at least one officer wearing a body camera. Critics noted the policy gives ICE broad discretion over public release of footage, limiting accountability.
content:
On July 15, 2026, DHS announced that every ICE arrest team would be required to include at least one officer equipped with a body-worn camera, following intense public and congressional pressure after two fatal shootings in which no body camera footage existed.

  • The mandate came after ICE agents fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston on July 7 and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine on July 13 — neither incident captured by body cameras.
  • Congress allocated $20 million for body camera procurement; ICE issued delivery orders totaling $30.9 million to Axon Enterprise on July 17 and July 20.
  • Acting ICE Director David Venturella stated all field agents would be equipped by end of August 2026.

The body-worn camera policy (ICE Directive 19010.3) grants the agency director broad discretion over release of footage from shootings and incidents involving death or serious injury, specifying that releases must be in ICE's "best interests." Critics and lawmakers said the policy undermines the accountability purpose of the cameras.

The Intercept had previously reported that ICE officers at the Maine shooting possessed body cameras they were unable to activate. Dozens of senators signed a letter stating: "In shooting after shooting, we are told that there is no body-worn camera footage of the incident and asked to accept DHS's account of the incident. Time and again, that account turns out to be a blatant falsehood."
source: CBS News / Time / Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette
